notes: USB maker string TTGK Technology, product string ECHO-A; HID interface 3 with reports 0x4B and 0x54, 64 B with report id; descriptor only, nothing sent (run:2026-10-21-moondrop-echo-a-01; scope-moondrop.md:134,160)

vid 0x3302 is the WalkPlay vendor id used by the WalkPlay driver code (core/WalkPlay.kt:22); that the PEQ protocol is WalkPlay SchemeNo11 was a hypothesis from the vendor id, the report ids and the WalkPlay cloud catalog row (Id 105, ECHO-A, brand MOONDROP, 8 channels); the 21.10.2026 PC read (run:2026-10-21-moondrop-echo-a-02, 11 read frames, nothing written) proves that the unit answers the Protocol Micro's read frames: firmware 0.1, 8 bands, the preamp, the slot byte. Write, flash commit and reset are still unproven on this unit

no vendor software shows the Echo-A: MOONDROP Hub has 0 hits for ECHO-A, the MOONDROP Link supported-products list has no ECHO-A, the product page declares no PEQ or app control, the QR-card app in the box is not identified (scope-moondrop.md:138-146); owner question 1 (scope-moondrop.md:198-199)
the advBeta Moondrop name rule 'Echo A' never matches the USB name ECHO-A (advbeta-reddit-astra@39c16e3:android/core/src/main/kotlin/io/github/chronosauros/contour/core/native/MoondropCatalog.kt:57)

reset.src: no vendor software for the Echo-A (scope-moondrop.md:168-170). The Protocol Micro code that drives it has the WalkPlay web tool's reset (decoded, walkplay-plan.md item 4): 01 03 02 00 00; eight flat PURE band frames (50/200/500/1000/2500/5000/10000/15000 Hz, Q 0.75, 0 dB, PK, length byte 0x18); 01 0A 04 00 00 FF FF; 01 01 00; 01 05 01..04; 01 17 00. Bench only (reset-plan echo-a --owner-consent, after a full backup); not in the app and not run on this unit; what it erases beyond the EQ is unknown

hwVolume.src: no vendor software controls it; the Windows UAC endpoint is hardware (-60..0 dB) but not vendor-driven, out of scope under the rule (scope-moondrop.md:172-174)

values: the Micro's code drives the Echo-A and its page offers a mic gain row
the Echo-A takes the write for some values only: PC FAIL (run:2026-10-22-moondrop-echo-a-01, RUN-EA4), phone 0 and +1 accepted, -1 ignored (run:2026-10-22-moondrop-echo-a-01-phone, run.md L96-106)
conflicts.resolution: read only in every build, review builds included: a write that the DAC takes only for some values is not offered (owner rule, 1.6 brief: mic Echo-A read only, as on the TRN)

values: walkplay (vendor id 0x3302, report ids 0x4B and 0x54, WalkPlay cloud catalog row Id 105, SchemeNo 11)
no vendor software lists the Echo-A at all
the unit answers the Protocol Micro's WalkPlay read frames (run:2026-10-21-moondrop-echo-a-02)
conflicts.resolution: walkplay, read path proven on the unit on 21.10.2026 (11 read frames: firmware 0.1, 8 bands, preamp, slot byte; the factory state is the Micro's flat PK 31..4000 Hz Q 0.75); write, commit and reset are not proven: nothing was written to the unit
8: the catalog row (scope-moondrop.md:162-165) and the PC read of 21.10.2026 agree - all eight bands answered
+-10 (the SchemeNo11 profile, scope-moondrop.md:155,163-165; Q 0.1-10 from the same profile, peq.q); no value from vendor software, none measured

values: PK, LS (WalkPlay SchemeNo11 row used by the Micro)
no shelves (devicePEQ Moondrop-name rule Echo A, which does not match the USB name)
conflicts.resolution: PK + LS + LP + HP as the SchemeNo11 profile lists them (scope-moondrop.md:155), plus HS emulated as the Micro does it (a LOW SHELF with the negated gain, the HS gain in the preamp); the sources disagree and none is vendor software, so the write is behind a verification flag (WalkPlayProfiles.ECHO_A_HARDWARE_VERIFIED, off) until the PC bench writes the unit; the 21.10.2026 PEQ read (run:2026-10-21-moondrop-echo-a-02) proved the read path only

values: 20-20000 Hz (the code applies the Protocol Micro's range to the Echo-A)
no source names a frequency range for the Echo-A
conflicts.resolution: open: stays "unknown" here; the code value is held in core/devices/PendingRecords.kt (ECHO_A_FREQ_HZ) until a read or capture gives one

values: none identified: Hub and Link do not list the Echo-A; the QR-card app is unknown
conflicts.resolution: open: owner question 1 (scan the QR card, or treat the WalkPlay catalog row as vendor software)

usb.pcBench: run:2026-10-21-moondrop-echo-a-01 and -02 HID descriptor: 3302:12C5, product ECHO-A, maker TTGK Technology, interface 3, 92 B descriptor, reports 0x4B and 0x54 (64 B with id); the descriptor itself sends nothing

bands.source: WalkPlay cloud catalog via the devicePEQ copy (entry Id 105 ECHO-A, 8 channels, SchemeNo 11, created 2024-11-29, updated 2024-12-18); a catalog row, not an app UI (scope-moondrop.md:143)
bands.pcBench: run:2026-10-21-moondrop-echo-a-02, read only (11 WalkPlay read frames, firmware command 0x0C = 0.1): 8 bands, all PK, 31/62/125/250/500/1000/2000/4000 Hz, Q 0.75 (192/256), gain 0, preamp 0 dB, slot byte 0 - the Protocol Micro's factory flat; no write, select, save, clear or reset frame was sent
bands.phone: run:2026-10-25-moondrop-echo-a-phone-nothing: PK, LS, LP, HP, HS and preamp VERIFIED, coefficients at 93 750 Hz, state after = start; the emulated HS ends 0.5 dB low when its gain is not a whole dB (the editor keeps it on a whole dB since round 6)
bands.acoustic: run:2026-10-25-moondrop-echo-a-05-mac-eqtest-48k (stream 48 kHz, firmware 0.1): PK mix, shelf mix with the emulated HS (level -5.997 / -6.000), preamp -6, LP 8000 Hz and HP all PASS; the DSP is fixed and does not follow the stream. WalkPlayProfiles.ECHO_A_HARDWARE_VERIFIED is true; the positive preamp, the reset and the mic row stay as they were

peq.coefficientRateHz.source: devicePEQ computeIIRFilter(..., a = 96e3) designs the coefficients for 96 kHz (the Protocol Micro code that drives the Echo-A does the same)
peq.coefficientRateHz.pcBench: the coefficient bytes Contour sent are in the HID logs of the runs (hid/NN-plan-slotactive.log), decoded and replayed at 96 000 and 93 750 Hz (dac-lab:contour-1.6/research/2026-10-24-dsp-model-walkplay.md)
peq.coefficientRateHz.acoustic: run:2026-10-24-moondrop-echo-a-03-mac-eqtest and run:2026-10-24-moondrop-echo-a-04-mac-eqtest (stream 44.1 kHz): the DSP plays the coefficient bytes at 93 750 Hz; with coefficients designed for 93 750 Hz every valid case fits within 0.057 dB, designed for 96 000 Hz PK Q5 and LP 8000 fail (0.73-0.88 and 0.56 dB). Shelves play the slope form Contour already uses (LS 3000 -5 Q 0.71 decides: slope 0.020 dB, register / sqrt2 0.339 dB), so the register Q of its shelves is not rescaled. Not checked at a 48 kHz stream
